purpose: Explain which identified evidence, legal-source, property-record, procedural or correction changes would trigger reassessment of an approved answer, without speculating that such a change will occur.
core_principle: CURRENT ANSWER → MATERIAL DEPENDENCY → CHANGE THAT MATTERS → REASSESSMENT TRIGGER
rules: Only actual dependencies of the approved answer are listed as material.
A possible future event is not presented as likely or certain.
A trigger means reassessment is required; it does not predetermine the new answer.
Evidence changes and legal-rule changes remain distinct.
Historical answers are reassessed only when relevant historical dependencies change.
A new record does not automatically change the answer unless its material effect is established.
A procedure change may alter next steps without changing the underlying legal conclusion.
A deadline change may alter action timing without changing ownership or title.
The citizen sees actionable conditions without speculative predictions.
hard_stops: Never predict that a future event will change the answer.
Never state a hypothetical new evidence result as fact.
Never treat every source update as material.
Never claim a legal change affects an answer without dependency analysis.
Never imply reassessment guarantees a different conclusion.
Never expose internal dependency graphs or reasoning.
